title: The integrated single-coax revision
bullets: 129 component instances in the revised assembly
One continuous coax; no gun-end SMA socket
Original head seals and coolant routes retained
speech: This is the integrated single coax revision of the Advanced Tinkering reconstruction. The revised assembly contains one hundred and twenty nine component instances. The power connection is now one continuous coax cable through the atmospheric service tube. There is no additional S M A socket on the gun. The original head seals and two reference coolant hose routes are retained. This is a mechanical integration study, not an electrically qualified sputtering source.

title: Cable route and preparation
bullets: Intact coax offsets below the coolant hoses
Exposed shield band is captured by the clamp
Protected center makes a quarter-turn to the lug
speech: The intact coax passes through the narrow K F sixteen neck, then offsets to the opposite side of the coolant hoses. Its modeled minimum bend radius in that offset is twenty five point four millimetres. Near the head, a short jacket removal exposes a nine millimetre shield band. The clamp contacts that band. Beyond it, the shield ends and the protected center conductor makes a seven point five millimetre radius quarter turn toward the live terminal. These preparation dimensions remain conditional on the cable selected.

title: The ground connection is integrated
bullets: Commercial clamp envelope: 8 x11.8 x13.6 mm
Conductive carrier bonds to grounded Boden
Blind anchor and mounting hardware included
speech: Here is the ground connection with its mounting hardware included. The clamp study reserves the published eight by eleven point eight by thirteen point six millimetre envelope of the icotek S K L three to six clamp. Its spring shape is representative, not supplier C A D. A conductive carrier supports it and seats against the grounded Boden. A separate blind anchor stays on the dry cavity side. The clamp screw, nut, carrier and anchor have all been included in the mechanical checks. The body still requires a verified chamber ground bond.

title: A ring terminal that actually fits
bullets: 8.74 mm terminal is wider than original 8 mm passage
Copper stand-off brings the connection behind the yoke
M4 x20 screw retains the ring terminal
speech: The real ring terminal is wider than the original terminal passage through the steel yoke. Instead of cutting a slot near the magnets, this revision adds a copper stand off through that existing passage. It brings the contact behind the yoke. A longer M four by twenty screw retains the ring terminal and engages the original copper bore. The modeled engagement is six point seven one millimetres, leaving one point two nine millimetres before the source bore end. The terminal barrel points toward the entering cable, avoiding a tight return loop.

title: Insulation and coolant clearance
bullets: RF center and shield follow separate connections
Dielectric and guard sleeve protect the center
Coolant hoses remain clear of the new hardware
speech: The center conductor connects to the live copper assembly. The shield connects to the grounded bottom body. Cable dielectric and an additional guard sleeve protect the transition between those points. The main P T F E ring continues to isolate the live spacer from the Boden. The two blue coolant hoses follow their original reference routes. The new hardware clears those hoses in the solid model. The ring terminal and clamp are dimensioned study models; their actual purchased forms and electrical ratings still need confirmation.

title: What changed and what was checked
bullets: Separate revision; original source files preserved
One-inch tube with the original KF16 capture geometry
Mechanical checks do not establish RF ratings
speech: The revision changes the power termination, adds the internal ground anchor and replaces the service tube with a one inch tube while preserving the narrow K F sixteen capture geometry near the head. The original source files remain untouched. The reported contacts distinguish nominal screw threads, spring pressure on the braid and the formed ground saddle interface from unwanted collisions. This video shows the integrated geometry. It does not establish operating power, R F voltage clearance, spring performance or cooling capability. Those require the selected components and prototype verification.
